record_verbatim.objective: Confirm that when a genuine overvoltage reaction occurs while the vehicle is being driven, the outcome is the one the end-user driver stakeholder needs: the pack is isolated, the vehicle coasts to a stop under its own control, and the driver is told what happened in terms that do not require a diagnostic engineer to interpret. This measure exists because the master prompt warns that disconnecting a battery can itself affect propulsion: the safety reaction that satisfies the safety goal may still fail the stakeholder if the driver is left without an explanation.

oracle_detail.what_the_oracle_is_not: It is not a measured reference: no vehicle has been driven and no driver has been observed. It is not an analytical model: nothing here models the vehicle's coast behaviour, which the real judge would be. It is not a requirement test: FB2-VER-TMS-000006 and FB2-VER-EXE-000006 exercise the state machine's reaction, which says the state changes and not that a human understands what changed.
oracle_detail.why_this_oracle: Two oracles are combined and both are declared. The safety half is a source-grounded oracle: the 100 ms figure comes from the safety goal's own FTTI and is checkable by arithmetic against the timing budget. The experience half is a synthetic-assumption oracle: 'actionable to a driver' has no agreed definition in this corpus, and the proposal that it is decided by asking the driver class is a process invention, not a derived criterion.

preconditions: The pack, vehicle and charger are real (hypothetical) installations, not a bench.
A driver representative from the declared end-user class is available and has not been briefed on what the item will do.
A logging setup captures the driver-facing indication, not only the internal state.
record_verbatim.regression_selection: Re-run whenever the fault-reaction logic, the state indication, the latching policy or the mode arbitration changes. It is the only measure that tests whether the mode-dependent reaction is comprehensible, so it is never sampled out.

signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
